text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government has sent medical personnel and supplies to the southern town of Maamba after heavy flooding in the area last week.
- Defence Minister Ben Mwila told parliament the government did not plan trimming the size of its army because there was no guarantee that continued peace would prevail.
- The finance ministry has authorised increased pay for magistrates after a two-day strike.
- Suspended Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa chief, Bingu Wa Mutharika, said he will not recognise a verdict of a committee appointed to probe charges agiant him of financial abuses.
- Opposition National Party leader Humphrey Mulemba has denied reports that he had resigned from the party and has asked members to ignore the rumour.

- A journalist from The Post has been detained for making a citizens arrest of an intelligence officer apparently masquerading as a journalist at a news conference called by Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) chief Bingu Wa Mutharia.
